summary.core_axiom: The body knows before the law finishes speaking.
summary.motion_model: spark -> stomp -> riot choice -> impact -> aftershock
summary.tier_note: Guild-core, mechanic-core, structural-anchor, commander-structural-anchor, and mono-color structural anchors are intentionally separated to avoid flattening Gruul into generic red-green stompy.

cards.secondary_signal: the biggest voice becomes law
cards.vox_mana_read: The clan does not debate the mountain; it follows the thing that can move it.
cards.why_canonical: Original Gruul parun and mythic-scale embodiment of clan force.

cards.secondary_signal: every drawn land can become a thrown boulder
cards.vox_mana_read: Even the ground is not passive when Gruul anger picks it up.
cards.why_canonical: Signature Gruul commander turning lands and combat damage into destructive reach.

cards.secondary_signal: noncreature plans become self-harm
cards.combat_axis: must attack each combat if able
cards.vox_mana_read: Every clever plan pays a blood toll before it gets to matter.
cards.why_canonical: Iconic Gruul maze runner; clean anti-control and creature-combat identity.

cards.secondary_signal: mana doubles when the deck commits to bodies
cards.vox_mana_read: Power comes when the deck stops asking permission from anything that is not alive.
cards.why_canonical: Ravnica Allegiance Gruul leader representing anti-spell creature primacy.

cards.primary_signal: the riot has a tactician, barely
cards.secondary_signal: cards and fights both favor creature density
cards.vox_mana_read: Gruul card advantage is not study; it is finding the next thing willing to charge.
cards.why_canonical: First Domri card; aligns Gruul with creature density and fight removal.

cards.secondary_signal: mana and riot turn the next body into immediate pressure
cards.vox_mana_read: The crowd does not wait for a plan when the next monster can arrive angry.
cards.why_canonical: Ravnica Allegiance Domri directly references riot and creature acceleration.

cards.secondary_signal: every creature enters with more force and fewer questions
cards.vox_mana_read: The strongest argument in the room is the one that survives the fight.
cards.why_canonical: Domri's War of the Spark card is a compact Gruul package: mana, creature boost, fight.

cards.primary_signal: the wild refuses to be denied
cards.secondary_signal: creatures either arrive bigger or arrive now
cards.vox_mana_read: Gruul does not ask if the creature resolves; it asks whether it hits now or hits harder later.
cards.why_canonical: Riot support card and classic Gruul anti-control enchantment.

cards.secondary_signal: haste or size is chosen at entry
cards.vox_mana_read: A Gruul answer to control is a body that arrives before the rules can catch it.
cards.why_canonical: Featured example for riot in Ravnica Allegiance and a defining efficient Gruul threat.

cards.mechanical_role: riot finisher / fight or land destruction
cards.secondary_signal: the creature chooses speed or size, then removes an obstacle
cards.vox_mana_read: When a Gruul finisher enters, something in the way stops being in the way.
cards.why_canonical: Ravnica Allegiance Gruul rare that ties riot to obstacle removal.

cards.secondary_signal: haste pressure or counter growth
cards.vox_mana_read: The first decision is already a charge: hit now or become harder to stop.
cards.why_canonical: Clean low-cost riot example for onboarding the mechanic.

cards.secondary_signal: spells and artifacts become liabilities
cards.vox_mana_read: Every delicate machine catches fire when the wild gets close enough.
cards.why_canonical: Modern Gruul sideboard-style identity: punish spells and break artifacts/enchantments.

cards.secondary_signal: one spell hits flyer, ground body, and player
cards.combat_axis: clears blockers and pressures life total
cards.vox_mana_read: Gruul does not choose one target when the whole battlefield is an insult.
cards.why_canonical: Signature Gatecrash Gruul spell showing scalable violence across board layers.

cards.primary_signal: the clan chooses the route through
cards.secondary_signal: blockers, flyers, and stolen bodies all become problems to solve
cards.vox_mana_read: A Gruul charm is not subtle utility; it is a way to clear the charge lane.
cards.why_canonical: Named Gruul charm and flexible expression of combat-first utility.

cards.primary_signal: the chant makes a crowd into a stampede
cards.secondary_signal: all bodies become louder and harder to block
cards.vox_mana_read: The song is not inspiration; it is the sound of a street becoming a herd.
cards.why_canonical: Named Gruul anthem that turns board presence into difficult combat math.

cards.secondary_signal: lands become attackers and creatures gain trample
cards.vox_mana_read: Gruul does not stand on land; it wakes the land up and sends it forward.
cards.why_canonical: Guildmage names Skarrg and captures Gruul's trample/land animation identity.

cards.secondary_signal: a creature enters and pays for the next motion
cards.vox_mana_read: The riot is strongest when each body pays for the next body.
cards.why_canonical: Iconic Gruul hybrid creature that enables explosive creature chains.

cards.secondary_signal: non-mana activation becomes pain
cards.vox_mana_read: Every little lever in the city has thorns on it when Gruul is watching.
cards.why_canonical: Original Ravnica Gruul card punishing fiddly activated abilities.

cards.secondary_signal: the clan grows while opponents feel the pulse
cards.vox_mana_read: Even Gruul ramp is not peaceful; the mana comes with a bruise.
cards.why_canonical: Named Zhur-Taa card joining ramp with direct damage.

cards.primary_signal: the creature can become a moment of impact
cards.secondary_signal: body in hand turns an attacker into a breakthrough
cards.vox_mana_read: Sometimes the monster is not cast; it is thrown into the attack already happening.
cards.why_canonical: Most famous bloodrush card and core Gruul combat-translation anchor.

cards.secondary_signal: lands turn into power during combat
cards.vox_mana_read: The more ground Gruul holds, the harder the swing lands.
cards.why_canonical: Bloodrush card that converts land count into attack force.

cards.primary_signal: each attacker makes the leader larger
cards.secondary_signal: wide pressure becomes tall pressure
cards.vox_mana_read: The more the clan charges, the bigger the charge leader becomes.
cards.why_canonical: Named Rubblebelt Gruul creature connecting attacking to growth.

cards.primary_signal: red side of Gruul combat translation
cards.secondary_signal: card in hand becomes sudden force
cards.vox_mana_read: A body can be a creature later or a roar right now.
cards.why_canonical: Mono-red bloodrush example that still belongs to the Gruul mechanic family.

cards.primary_signal: green side of Gruul combat translation
cards.secondary_signal: stored muscle becomes combat growth
cards.vox_mana_read: The wild does not need a spell to make the attack larger.
cards.why_canonical: Mono-green bloodrush example showing Gruul's creature/spell boundary blur.

cards.primary_signal: the biggest body can become the biggest swing
cards.secondary_signal: threat in hand becomes lethal combat math
cards.vox_mana_read: Sometimes the endgame is not casting the giant; it is letting the giant inhabit the attacker.
cards.why_canonical: Large mono-green bloodrush expression tied to Skarrg/Gruul naming.

cards.primary_signal: small wild things change huge decisions
cards.secondary_signal: one green card turns any attacker into a dangerous blocker problem
cards.vox_mana_read: Gruul force is not only size; it is the certainty that contact matters.
cards.why_canonical: Efficient bloodrush card demonstrating combat leverage beyond raw stats.

cards.secondary_signal: red body converts to sudden attacking power
cards.vox_mana_read: The creature is optional; the damage is the point.
cards.why_canonical: Mono-red bloodrush card representing burst-force mode.

cards.primary_signal: one discarded body can double the ending
cards.secondary_signal: combat trick turns pressure into kill threat
cards.vox_mana_read: Gruul does not just hit harder; it hits again before the table finishes understanding the first hit.
cards.why_canonical: Bloodrush finisher that translates a creature card into lethal combat compression.

cards.secondary_signal: simple large pump or creature
cards.vox_mana_read: There is no hidden layer here; it is either a boar or the force of a boar.
cards.why_canonical: Named Zhur-Taa bloodrush common for baseline mechanic readability.

cards.secondary_signal: bloodrush changes who survives combat
cards.vox_mana_read: The wild does not need patience; it needs the first bite to matter.
cards.why_canonical: Mono-red bloodrush card showing keyword-based combat translation.

cards.primary_signal: the trick comes back after impact
cards.secondary_signal: combat investment can return from graveyard
cards.vox_mana_read: Gruul momentum is not careful recursion; it is the same shove coming back for another swing.
cards.why_canonical: Dragon's Maze bloodrush card that adds recursive combat pressure.

cards.secondary_signal: the second hit arrives larger because the first hit landed
cards.vox_mana_read: Gruul asks one question first: has someone already been hurt? Good. Now grow.
cards.why_canonical: Classic Guildpact bloodthirst creature and early Gruul pressure example.

cards.primary_signal: small creature scales after first blood
cards.secondary_signal: damage makes even the smallest body hard to block
cards.vox_mana_read: Once the first wound opens, even the small fighters know where to slip through.
cards.why_canonical: Guildpact bloodthirst card tied to Skarrg/Gruul naming and early momentum.

cards.secondary_signal: opponent damage turns graveyard access into pressure
cards.vox_mana_read: The fire comes back because the fight is still warm.
cards.why_canonical: Bloodthirst rare demonstrating Gruul pressure that reappears if damage keeps happening.

cards.primary_signal: the environment itself shakes damage loose
cards.secondary_signal: everyone takes pressure whether they negotiate or not
cards.vox_mana_read: The slum does not attack first; the world around it starts hurting.
cards.why_canonical: Original Gruul rare: big efficient body plus unavoidable pressure.

cards.primary_signal: first blood makes the fighter disruptive
cards.secondary_signal: damage unlocks control over blocks
cards.vox_mana_read: After blood is drawn, Gruul starts deciding who is allowed to stand in the way.
cards.why_canonical: Guildpact bloodthirst card showing post-damage combat manipulation.

cards.secondary_signal: mana base turns any body into a trampler
cards.vox_mana_read: Gruul territory is not neutral ground; it teaches creatures how to hit through.
cards.why_canonical: Original Gruul guild land and named Skarrg anchor.

cards.primary_signal: the mana base has a footprint
cards.secondary_signal: Gruul starts with ground that hurts
cards.vox_mana_read: The first Gruul choice is often whether the ground should hurt now so the deck can move faster.
cards.why_canonical: Canonical Gruul shock land and Commander mana-base anchor.

cards.primary_signal: territory is lifted and slammed back down
cards.secondary_signal: one land drop stores more future force
cards.vox_mana_read: Gruul can pause only if the next step lands heavier.
cards.why_canonical: Original Ravnica Gruul bounceland and common mana-base identity piece.

cards.secondary_signal: red and green bodies determine its initial mass
cards.combat_axis: counters convert into damage or tokens
cards.vox_mana_read: A Gruul monster is born from the number of bodies already willing to be near it.
cards.maze_query_seed: ci=gruul commander o:+1/+1 counter o:damage o:Saproling
cards.why_canonical: Original Ravnica-era Gruul legendary for body-count scaling and conversion.

cards.secondary_signal: resources are built to become enormous effects
cards.vox_mana_read: Gruul math is simple: make the X large enough that nobody cares how elegant the equation was.
cards.why_canonical: Hybrid red-green commander often used for hydras and oversized X-spells.

cards.primary_signal: more land means more routes and bigger movement
cards.secondary_signal: land drops and trample turn terrain into velocity
cards.vox_mana_read: The wildborn do not hold territory; they turn it into forward motion.
cards.why_canonical: Popular red-green land commander that fits Gruul terrain-to-combat translation.

cards.secondary_signal: the attack step becomes resource phase
cards.vox_mana_read: Gruul does not ramp before combat; sometimes combat is the ramp.
cards.why_canonical: Classic red-green legend joining attack pressure to mana production.

cards.primary_signal: the land tells the next move
cards.secondary_signal: terrain on top of library becomes playable force
cards.resource_axis: lands as card access and power
cards.vox_mana_read: Radha reads the ground ahead and swings with every piece of it behind her.
cards.why_canonical: Modern Radha commander for land-driven combat scaling.

cards.set_context: Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur's Gate
cards.secondary_signal: mana dorks become attackers and giant spells become finishers
cards.vox_mana_read: The workers who make the mana also know how to throw a punch.
cards.why_canonical: Commander anchor that literally converts mana creatures into Gruul combat pressure.

cards.secondary_signal: one body becomes a sudden lethal event
cards.vox_mana_read: The party is over when one creature becomes the entire stampede.
cards.why_canonical: Premier Gruul Commander payoff for haste and oversized attacks.

cards.secondary_signal: board presence makes mana and hasty bodies
cards.vox_mana_read: A revel is just ramp if enough bodies show up.
cards.why_canonical: Red-green planeswalker translating creature density into mana and hasty pressure.

cards.secondary_signal: dragons become lethal through combat multiplication
cards.vox_mana_read: Gruul does not leave the sky to blue; it fills it with teeth.
cards.maze_query_seed: ci=gruul commander t:dragon o:attacking o:double strike
cards.why_canonical: Iconic red-green Dragon commander for combat multiplication.

cards.secondary_signal: one body enters and burns the obstacles away
cards.vox_mana_read: The predator does not ask for a clear lane; it clears the lane by landing.
cards.why_canonical: Powerful red-green elder dragon expressing big threat plus removal on entry.

cards.primary_signal: the swing funds the next swing
cards.secondary_signal: attacking makes a burst of red-green mana
cards.vox_mana_read: In Gruul, a dragon attack is also a ritual.
cards.why_canonical: Staple red-green attack-mana engine and Commander combo/combat anchor.

cards.secondary_signal: fights and blocked power generate advantage
cards.vox_mana_read: Gruul card draw is the record kept by whatever survived the fight.
cards.why_canonical: Commander anchor for fight, power, and combat-based card advantage.

cards.primary_signal: destiny feeds from what already happened
cards.secondary_signal: graveyards become mana or damage
cards.vox_mana_read: Even Gruul can be patient when destiny itself keeps burning the old fuel.
cards.why_canonical: Red-green god that adds inexorable resource/damage pressure beyond pure combat.

cards.secondary_signal: terrain creates elementals and dead elementals throw damage
cards.vox_mana_read: When the land itself is furious, every new place becomes another body in the fight.
cards.why_canonical: Major red-green Commander landfall payoff aligning terrain, bodies, and damage.

cards.mechanical_role: ETB spell theft / transformed poison titan
cards.secondary_signal: arrival converts every player's top card into Gruul momentum
cards.vox_mana_read: The predator does not draw from a library; it eats the top of everyone else's.
cards.why_canonical: Modern red-green color-identity commander with massive ETB and apex threat posture.

cards.primary_signal: the deck discounts large bodies and rewards attacking
cards.secondary_signal: green muscle supports Gruul top-end
cards.vox_mana_read: Goreclaw is the green half of Gruul saying: make them huge, then make them trample.
cards.why_canonical: Mono-green commander useful as a Gruul-adjacent big-creature/ramp anchor.

cards.primary_signal: existing power calls a larger predator
cards.secondary_signal: board strength turns into cheaper apex threat
cards.vox_mana_read: The more force already on the board, the cheaper the largest force becomes.
cards.maze_query_seed: ci<=gruul commander o:costs less o:power o:trample
cards.why_canonical: Mono-green apex creature that cleanly expresses Gruul's power-scaling finisher logic.

source_notes: Scryfall exact-title links are included per row for card lookup.
Official Wizards articles anchor riot, bloodrush, bloodthirst, and red-green/Gruul philosophy.
Matrix is intended as a source-of-truth seed for Vox Mana placement panels, commander dossier sections, and Maze search families.
